summary: This note describes professional basketball in the New York metropolitan area, centered on Madison Square Garden and the Barclays Center. It traces the New York Nets from their ABA days, when they shared Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum with the Islanders and won two ABA titles with Julius Erving, through their move to New Jersey and later to Brooklyn in 2012.
one_line: Overview of professional basketball in New York, including the Knicks, Liberty, Brooklyn Nets and the history of the Nets franchise.
key_facts: New Yorkers can watch the New York Knicks play NBA basketball at Madison Square Garden.
The New York Liberty play in the WNBA at Madison Square Garden.
The Barclays Center in Brooklyn is home to the Brooklyn Nets NBA basketball team.
The Brooklyn Nets began playing in Brooklyn in 2012.
The Nets' arrival in Brooklyn made them the first major professional sports team to play in the historic borough in half a century.
Before the 1976 -- 1977 NBA merger, the New York Nets were a two-time champion in the American Basketball Association (ABA).
The New York Nets shared Nassau Veterans Memorial Coliseum on Long Island with the NHL's New York Islanders.
Julius Erving, a famous Hall of Fame forward, starred for the New York Nets.
During the first season of the merger (1976 -- 77), the Nets continued to play on Long Island.
Erving's contract had been sold to the Philadelphia 76ers by the first season of the merger.
The Nets transferred to New Jersey the next season and became known as the New Jersey Nets.
The New Jersey Nets later moved to Brooklyn prior to the 2012 -- 2013 NBA season.
